1	# WP-005: Expose `projectExists` flag and gate "View Project" button
     2	
     3	## Plan Context
     4	
     5	Polish the orchestrator GUI run queue view with five targeted fixes including hiding the "View Project" button until the project ledger actually exists.
     6	
     7	## Description
     8	
     9	Add a `projectExists: boolean` field to the `QueueEntry` interface and populate it in `getQueue()`, then update the frontend to gate the "View Project" button on this authoritative flag instead of inferring visibility from `effectiveStatus`. Include a unit test verifying the new field.
    10	
    11	## Scope
    12	
    13	- `mcp-server/src/gui/queue/types.ts` — extend `QueueEntry` interface
    14	- `mcp-server/src/gui/queue/get-queue.ts` — populate `projectExists` in the enriched result object
    15	- `mcp-server/gui/public/views/orchestrator.js` — change "View Project" button condition
    16	- `mcp-server/tests/gui/queue/` — new or updated test file for `getQueue()` covering `projectExists`
    17	
    18	## Deliverables
    19	
    20	- `QueueEntry` interface includes `projectExists: boolean` field with JSDoc comment
    21	- `getQueue()` sets `projectExists` from the already-computed `projectStatus.exists` value (line ~155 of `get-queue.ts`)
    22	- "View Project" button rendered only when `entry.projectExists === true && entry.expectedSlug` (replacing the current `status === 'started' && entry.expectedSlug` condition at line ~266 of `orchestrator.js`)
    23	- Unit test asserting `projectExists: true` when a ledger exists and `projectExists: false` when it does not
    24	
    25	## Dependencies
    26	
    27	- None
    28	
    29	## Acceptance Criteria
    30	
    31	1. The `QueueEntry` interface in `types.ts` includes a `projectExists: boolean` field.
    32	2. `getQueue()` populates `projectExists` from `projectStatus.exists` for every returned entry.
    33	3. The "View Project" button is NOT rendered when `projectExists` is `false`, even if `effectiveStatus === 'started'`.
    34	4. The "View Project" button IS rendered when `projectExists` is `true` and `entry.expectedSlug` is truthy.
    35	5. A unit test covers both the `projectExists: true` and `projectExists: false` cases for `getQueue()` output.
    36	6. Existing tests continue to pass without modification (no regressions).
    37

    39	
    40	`implementation` → `qa` → `code-review` → `documentation`
    41

    43	
    44	Medium
    45	
    46	## Rationale
    47	
    48	The backend already computes `projectStatus.exists` in `getQueue()` (destructured at line ~155) but does not include it in the response. Exposing it as a dedicated field is authoritative and zero-cost, avoiding heuristic guessing on the frontend. This follows the existing pattern of extending `QueueEntry` with computed fields (`effectiveStatus`, `progress`, `lastAction`, `logFilename`).

    51	
    52	- *Infer from `effectiveStatus` alone* — `effectiveStatus` can transition to `'started'` before the ledger exists (when process is alive + has stage activity), producing a broken link. Not authoritative.
    53	- *Poll the project API from the frontend* — Adds an extra round-trip per queue entry per poll cycle for information the backend already has. Wasteful and racy.
    54

    56	
    57	The `projectExists` value is already computed in `get-queue.ts` — this WP is primarily about threading it through the `QueueEntry` interface and updating the frontend condition. 1	# WP-003: Preserve scroll position across queue refresh cycles
     2	
     3	## Plan Context
     4	
     5	Polish the orchestrator GUI run queue view with five targeted fixes including preserving scroll position across queue refresh cycles so the page doesn't jump back to the top every 5 seconds.
     6	
     7	## Description
     8	
     9	The `renderQueueTable` function replaces `container.innerHTML` on every 5-second polling cycle, destroying the DOM tree and resetting the page scroll to the top. Fix by saving `window.scrollY` before the innerHTML replacement and restoring it immediately after all post-render DOM manipulation.
    10	
    11	## Scope
    12	
    13	- `mcp-server/gui/public/views/orchestrator.js` — `renderQueueTable` function
    14	
    15	## Deliverables
    16	
    17	- Scroll-position save/restore logic wrapping the innerHTML replacement and subsequent DOM manipulation in `renderQueueTable`
    18	
    19	## Dependencies
    20	
    21	- None
    22	
    23	## Acceptance Criteria
    24	
    25	1. Scrolling down the queue page and waiting for a 5-second refresh cycle does not reset the viewport to the top.
    26	2. `window.scrollY` is used as the save/restore target (not `container.scrollTop`, since `#orch-queue-container` has no overflow CSS — the viewport is the scrolling context).
    27	3. The scroll position is restored after all post-render DOM manipulation (action button injection, event listener attachment) completes, not just after the innerHTML assignment.
    28	
    29	## Active Pipeline Stages
    30	
    31	`implementation` → `qa` → `code-review` → `documentation`
    32	
    33	## Estimated Complexity
    34	
    35	Low
    36	
    37	## Rationale
    38	
    39	Save/restore `window.scrollY` is preferred over incremental DOM updates because: (a) it's a 2-line change, (b) it has no behavioural risk, and (c) the queue table is small enough (< 20 rows) that full re-rendering is not a performance concern. The viewport, not the container, is the scrolling element since `#orch-queue-container` has no overflow CSS.
    40	
    41	## Rejected Approaches
    42	
    43	- *`container.scrollTop`* — Wrong target. The container has no `overflow` or `max-height` CSS, so it's not the scrolling element; the document viewport is.
    44	- *Incremental DOM diffing* — Disproportionate complexity for a table with < 20 rows. The innerHTML re-render is fast; the only problem is scroll position loss, which save/restore solves trivially.
    45	- *Virtual DOM library* — Introduces a new dependency and build complexity for a vanilla JS project. Out of scope per project constraints (no new npm dependencies).
    46	
    47	## Notes
    48	
    49	The save point should be at the start of `renderQueueTable` (before `container.innerHTML = html` at line ~252 of `orchestrator.js`). The restore point should be at the very end of the function, after all `entries.forEach` loops that inject action buttons, start log previews, and attach toggle listeners. This ensures the scroll position is not overwritten by intermediate DOM mutations.
